_note: Labelled intent set. One JSON object per line; lines beginning with a `_schema` key are metadata and are skipped by the loader. Fixed context: user demo@alphalaw.test, tz America/New_York, work_week_start 1, now 2026-08-20T13:12:04Z (Thursday, ISO week 34). Fields: id, query, lang, tags, context, expected{intent, services, entity_keys, entities, has_write, flag_ambiguity, refs_prior_turn, route}. `entity_keys` is what is graded; `entities` carries values only where the value is a literal lift from the query and is graded separately as entity-value accuracy. `route` is the front-door path we expect and is reported, not scored as accuracy.

query: What's on my calendar next week?
note: Brief single-service sample #1. Rule router owns it: one op, one window, one ordering. 0 LLM calls.

query: what do I have on Friday
note: Bare weekday, no 'next'. Resolves to the coming Friday inside this ISO week.

query: cal next wk?
note: Telegraphic. The rule router's literal patterns do not fire on abbreviations, so this costs one planner call. Getting the intent right here is the point; getting it right for free is not.

query: ¿Qué tengo en el calendario la próxima semana?
note: Spanish. The rule router is English-literal by construction, so the planner takes it.

query: 来週の予定を教えて
note: Japanese, no whitespace tokens. Also the case where the Postgres 'english' text arm contributes nothing and the vector arm carries the retrieval.

query: What's on my calendar next week where john@company.com is invited?
note: Problem statement example #3. An address is present, so 'John' needs no disambiguation — the router's boundary test is whether an @ is in the string.

query: Next Tuesday

prior_turns: What's on my calendar next week?

note: Brief hard case #3. A bare time phrase is not a query on its own; it carries the previous run's intent with a new window. On Thursday of ISO week 34, 'next Tuesday' is 2026-08-25 — the following ISO week, not the next occurrence.

query: Next Tuesday
note: Same string, empty conversation. The router declines and the planner defaults to calendar_list, because a naked date serves no other intent. Paired with i007 on purpose: the label depends on the conversation, not the string.

query: Find emails from sarah@company.com about the budget
note: Brief single-service sample #2. Exact sender prefilter plus a semantic topic.

query: any mail from acme about the renewal
note: Brand name, not an address. The alias table expands 'acme' to a sender domain and a token set before the probe runs.

query: emails sarah budget
note: Three nouns, no verb, no address. person_hint rather than from_email is the correct call — 'sarah' is not a sender until something resolves it.

query: Show me messages from legal@acmecorp.com in the last week
note: Sender plus a trailing window. 'last week' is the previous ISO week, half-open.

query: Trouve les e-mails de sarah@company.com à propos du budget
note: French of i009. The address survives translation, which is why the sender prefilter still bites.

query: did anyone send me the redlines
note: No sender, no window, one noun. Retrieval carries the whole query.

query: That email about the proposal

prior_turns: Prepare for tomorrow's meeting with Acme Corp

note: Brief hard case #2. Resolved against conversation_entities, not by re-searching the mailbox. If the referent was never surfaced this resolves wrongly and nothing detects it — the known limit.

query: open the Turkish Airlines booking email
note: 'Open' asks for the message itself, so the answer style is template:email_detail rather than prose.

query: show me the second one

prior_turns: Find emails from sarah@company.com about the budget

note: An ordinal into the previous turn's rendered list. Ambiguous only if the previous turn showed nothing.

query: Show me PDFs in Drive from last month
note: Brief single-service sample #3. sync_gdrive has no created date, so 'from last month' means modified last month and the answer says so.

query: spreadsheets in drive
note: A file-type word with no window. Pure metadata filter, no window to resolve.

query: pdfs last month
note: Two nouns. 'Drive' is not named and must be inferred from the file type.

query: Zeig mir PDFs aus Drive vom letzten Monat
note: German of i018.

query: find the countersigned MSA
note: Semantic file lookup with no type or date filter. Separated from drive_filter because the plan shape differs: one ranked search, not a prefilter listing.

query: where is the out of office doc
note: The document half of the brief's conflict-detection sample, asked on its own.

query: acme proposal v4 in drive
note: Version number in the query. The filename evidence flag should fire here, which is what lifts it over FLOOR_READ regardless of cosine.

query: Prepare for tomorrow's meeting with Acme Corp
note: Brief multi-service sample #2. Three services with no edges between the search steps — the case the DAG exists for.

query: prep me for the acme review on Thursday
note: Names the event, not the date range. The calendar step anchors the other two.

query: brief me before my 10am
note: A clock time with no date. Reads as the next 10am, which is a live calendar read rather than a mirror read.

query: kal ki Acme meeting ke liye prep kar do
note: Romanised Hindi with an English noun in the middle. 'kal' is tomorrow. Tests that the time phrase survives a language the temporal scanner has no patterns for — the window has to come out of the planner, not the pre-pass.

query: Find events next week that conflict with my out-of-office doc
note: Brief multi-service sample #3. Two parallel reads and a pure-Python interval intersection on top.

query: does anything clash with my OOO next week
note: Abbreviation the vector arm handles and the text arm does not.

query: am I double booked on Thursday
note: Conflict detection inside one service — overlap between calendar events, no document involved. The service set is the discriminator against i029.

query: when am I free Thursday afternoon
note: The complement of a calendar list: gaps, not events. Same retrieval, different rendering, so it earns its own intent.

query: find a 30 minute slot next week with sarah.chen@acmecorp.com
note: Reads free/busy for one attendee. Not a write — nothing is booked until the user asks.

query: Summarise everything Acme sent me this month
note: Fan-out inside one op — fourteen bodies fetched by one step, not fourteen plan steps.

query: what did I miss today
note: No entities at all. 'Today' is a live-freshness window, so this one reads through rather than off the mirror.

query: give me a rundown of this week's emails from acmecorp.com
note: Domain rather than address. Distinguishing digest from email_search is the summarise verb, not the filters.

query: Cancel my Turkish Airlines flight
note: The brief's headline query. One booking above FLOOR_WRITE, so no card is needed for which one — only for whether to send. The PNR is a reference to the probe's extractor output, never retyped by the model.

query: Cancel my flight to Istanbul
note: Two bookings to Istanbul inside MARGIN of each other. The ambiguity is visible at plan time because the probe already ran, so ask.user is step one rather than a replan.

query: Türk Hava Yolları uçuşumu iptal et
note: Turkish. The English text arm scores zero and the alias group has to carry it — this is the escalation-ladder case, and the evidence flag comes from an alias token in the subject rather than from similarity.

query: i need to cancel that THY booking
note: IATA-style abbreviation plus a deictic. The referent is already a conversation entity, so no ambiguity card is warranted even though the query alone is underspecified.

query: Move the meeting with John
note: Brief hard case #1. Two unknowns — which John, and to when — asked in one form rather than two round trips. Missing this flag is the dangerous direction: the system would move a meeting nobody chose.

query: push my 1:1 with John Park to Friday
note: Same intent as i041 with both unknowns supplied. The pair is the test of whether the ambiguity flag tracks the query rather than the intent name.

query: reschedule the design review to next Tuesday at 2
note: 'Reschedule' without a notify clause is move_event, not reschedule_and_notify. The verb alone does not decide it — the presence of a second recipient-facing action does.

query: move it an hour later

prior_turns: what do I have on Friday

note: Relative move against a referent from the previous turn. One event in scope, so no card for which one; there is still a confirm card because it is a write.

query: Push my Acme review next Thursday to Friday 3pm and tell the attendees
note: Two writes with an enforced order: if the calendar update fails, the email announcing it must not go. One card, two confirms.

query: move the renewal review to Monday and let everyone know
note: 'Let everyone know' is the notify clause in plainer words. Same DAG as i045.

query: draft a reply to sarah saying the budget looks fine
note: A reply needs a thread to reply to, so this is a search followed by a draft. 'Draft' is still a write: it creates a Gmail draft, which is why it goes through actions.

query: send john the MSA
note: Two Johns in the corpus and neither is above FLOOR_WRITE. Clearing the write floor is necessary and not sufficient — the margin has to clear too.

query: email the acme team the agenda for Thursday
note: Recipients come from the event's attendee list, so the calendar read is a dependency of the draft rather than a parallel step.

query: book 30 minutes with mike.ross@acmecorp.com tomorrow afternoon
note: Distinguished from availability (i033) by the verb: 'find a slot' reads, 'book' writes.

query: add a dentist appointment next Wednesday at 9
note: No attendees, no retrieval. The probe still runs and returns nothing, which is the right answer and costs one embedding.

query: share the Q3 renewal proposal with sarah.chen@acmecorp.com
note: One file clearly above FLOOR_WRITE, one named recipient. Confirm card, then a single Drive permission write.

query: give john access to the MSA
note: Sharing a countersigned contract with the wrong John is the failure this flag exists to prevent.

query: thanks, that's perfect
note: Whole-message match against a closed pattern set. 0 LLM calls, 0 embeddings, ~12 ms.

query: thanks!
note: The short form.

query: thanks — also what's on Friday?
note: The eager-matcher trap. A chit-chat matcher that fires on a prefix silently drops the real request appended to a thank-you — a bad failure and an invisible one. Labelled calendar_list on purpose.

query: perfect, do the same for Northwind

prior_turns: Summarise everything Acme sent me this month

note: Gratitude plus an imperative plus a new entity. Chit-chat must decline; the previous intent is reused with one entity swapped.

query: send it
note: Approval of an open card. has_write is false because the run does not plan a write — it approves one that already exists as an actions row. 0 LLM calls.

query: not now
note: Declining a card. The action goes to cancelled, which the partial unique index permits to be re-created later.

query: the first one
note: An answer to an open choice card, which is matcher #1 and resumes the paused run at 0 LLM calls. Contrast with i017, where the same shape of phrase with no open card is a fresh email_detail query.

query: book me a flight to Istanbul next Friday
note: Looks exactly like cancel_flight and is not — nothing in the op registry books anything. Returns the answer verb, not a plan. The near-miss against i038 is the point.

query: what's the weather tomorrow
note: No service covers it. A resolvable time phrase must not drag it to calendar_list.

query: post this to Slack

prior_turns: Summarise everything Acme sent me this month

note: A resolvable referent and an unsupported destination. Refusing has to survive the referent resolving cleanly.
